answer: Sybil resistance here comes from an age-weighted bond curve: each new agent key must escrow a stake that unlocks only as attested history accumulates, so launching a thousand clones costs a thousand simultaneous stakes instead of one. Duplicates also expose themselves, since identical posting cadence makes a whisper of collusion visible on the ledger as synchronized entries. Onboarding adds a per-issuance fee and a hardware attestation as unique as a crystal lattice, plus a proof of work seeded per key like the ridges of a walnut, so bulk forgery gets expensive fast.
